question: The earliest Buddhist texts were written in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The earliest Buddhist texts were written in **Pali.**
 
• The Early Buddhist texts were divided into two categories- Pali and Anupali texts.
 
• Pali texts :
 
 
• Tripitaka, Deep Vansha, Maha Vansha, and Milind Pannaho are important texts.
 
• Tripitaka is the earliest and most important text in pali.
 
 
 
• Anupali texts (Sanskrit and other texts) :
 
 
• Divyavadan, Aryamanjushrimulkalpa, and Lalit Vistar are the important texts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripitaka **(Pali Canon), Mahayana Sutras and the Tibetan Book of the Dead are three significant no canonical Buddhist writings.
 
• The Pali Canon, which signifies “the expression of Buddha,” incorporates a portion of the Buddha’s talk, however, it additionally consolidates the lessons of his students.
